newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen off $0.50-$1.00- trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen off $0.50-$1.00- trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Wednesday were seen $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower with the weaker tone liked to abundant hog supplies, livestock dealers said.
A break from last week's winter storm and extreme cold in the Midwest allowed producers a chance to ship hogs held back by the weather before another storm moves in, dealers said.

Top prices for hogs delivered to plants in Iowa and southern Minnesota were seen at $53.00 to $53.50, sources there said. Top Illinois prices at plants were seen at $52.50 to $53.00 and in Indiana/Ohio at $52.00 to $52.50.
Marketings were so active Tuesday that at least one major packer in the interior Iowa/southern Minnesota area reported having enough hogs for Wednesday.
There was growing concern that livestock movement would be disrupted again Thursday and Friday by another winter storm moving into the western Corn Belt, sources said.

The storm was seen spreading three to six inches of snow across much of the Midwest Tuesday and Wednesday. Also, strong winds behind the storm could cause significant transportation problems, according to Weather Services Corporation.
Sub-zero temperatures also were expected Friday and Saturday mornings through much of the Midwest, according to WSC.
